title: City Average Temperatures
statement: You get n readings. Each reading is a city name and a whole-number temperature in Celsius. A city can appear many times. For each city, find the average of its temperatures. Round it to 1 decimal place, with halves rounded away from zero (0.25 becomes 0.3 and -0.25 becomes -0.3). Never print -0.0; print 0.0 instead. Print the cities sorted by name in normal string order, so uppercase letters come before lowercase.
inputFormat: The first line has n. Each of the next n lines has a city name, one space, and an integer temperature.
outputFormat: One line for each different city, sorted by name: the city, one space, and the average with exactly 1 decimal digit.
constraints: City names have 1 to 12 English letters, no spaces
Names are case-sensitive: Delhi and delhi are different cities
explanations: Delhi has 30 and 34, average 32.0. Mumbai has 32 and 29, average 30.5. Chennai has one reading. Output is sorted by name.
The three Pune readings add to 62. Divide by 3 to get 20.666..., which rounds to 20.7.
reference:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    total = {}
    count = {}
    for i in range(n):
        city = data[1 + 2 * i]
        t = int(data[2 + 2 * i])
        total[city] = total.get(city, 0) + t
        count[city] = count.get(city, 0) + 1
    out = []
    for city in sorted(total):
        s = total[city]
        k = count[city]
        # tenths = |s| * 10 / k, rounded half up, using integers only
        q = (abs(s) * 20 + k) // (2 * k)
        sign = "-" if (s < 0 and q > 0) else ""
        out.append("%s %s%d.%d" % (city, sign, q // 10, q % 10))
    print("\n".join(out))

main()
